subject.title: Feature: Silence Watchdog + Response Delivery Confirmation — runtime-enforced operator visibility

question: Should OpenClaw keep this issue as the umbrella for a cross-channel runtime visibility policy, or should maintainers designate narrower canonical issues for the silence-watchdog and delivery-confirmation halves?
rationale: The requested behavior adds new default channel-visible output, config shape, retry/alert semantics, and cross-channel ACK expectations; source inspection can prove the gap, but cannot choose those product and compatibility defaults safely.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Work
options.body: Use this issue to coordinate policy while implementing bounded slices through the existing task-watchdog, durable-final-delivery, and delivery-failure-notification tracks.

options.title: Design One Combined Core Feature
options.body: Specify one default-on core contract here before implementation starts, including config, threshold, retry, alert, and channel ACK semantics.

options.title: Close After Canonical Split
options.body: Close this only after maintainers explicitly name the open issues that fully own both the silence-watchdog and delivery-confirmation halves.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Work
recommendation.body: Use this issue to coordinate policy while implementing bounded slices through the existing task-watchdog, durable-final-delivery, and delivery-failure-notification tracks.

likelyOwner.reason: The durable final fallback issue is the clearest maintainer-authored contract for the delivery-confirmation half and is closest to the unresolved product decision.
